title: Lanecrest Health - Health debrief & prioritization sync
summary: Quarterly health check focused on recent cost spike, two incidents in November, roadmap asks for model rollouts and private deployment considerations. Agreed on a pilot for dedicated capacity and security docs to be sent; prioritized action items for test harness and cost quick wins.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-30
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Notes: Recording enabled

Attendees:
- Sofia Patel (Redwood AE)
- Marcus Li (Redwood SE)
- Jordan Kim (Redwood CSM)
- Aisha Malik (Lanecrest, Head of ML)
- Tom Reyes (Lanecrest, CTO)
- Priya Anand (Lanecrest, SRE)
- Ben Ortiz (Product)
- Maya Singh (Lanecrest, Security)
- Chris (Data Eng - joined 00:14)

Auto-summary (auto-generated - may be incomplete):
Lanecrest saw a usage/cost anomaly in early Nov tied to unexpected batch job. Two reliability incidents (latency p99) triggered rollbacks. Customer exploring dedicated capacity for predictable p99 and data isolation; security wants SOC2 scope and KMS integration before private deploy. Redwood proposed immediate cost tweaks (smaller batch windows, prefix caching) and a 4-week dedicated pilot.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Patel: hey everyone thanks for joining on a Tuesday afternoon, uh we're gonna run through the lanecrest health debrief and then prioritize next steps, if anyone has a hard stop shout now, otherwise we'll go for ~45-50 minutes, okay?
[00:12] Aisha Malik: thanks Sofia yeah we should have until about 4:10 my side, that works. quick context: since the last qbr we had a couple of things - a cost spike and two incidents, so want to make sure we cover root causes and what the runway looks like.
[00:25] Marcus Li: yep, i'll start with the telemetry snapshot and then we can hand off to tom for the infra perspective. quick note - some of the labels in the dashboard spell 'KV cache' as "KV cash" in the export so ignore that if you see it.
[00:37] Tom Reyes: yeah, and chris will drop the trace link in chat once he's in. the short version: on 2027-11-12 we saw p95 ok but p99 went from 120ms to 1.2s for about 18 minutes during peak, which forced our app team to fallback model and that caused a user-facing delay.
[00:52] Priya Anand: to add, that 1.2s was correlated with a burst of long-context prompts from the nightly scoring job that ran concurrently with peak traffic, we didn't have the batching window configured to handle it.
[01:12] Marcus Li: exactly. the runtime saw a sudden sequence length bump — so kernel selection and memory pressure kicked in. we have three levers: smaller batching windows (cut q), prefix caching for repeated prompts, and dedicated capacity to guarantee headroom.
[01:30] Ben Ortiz: can you give us ballpark on cost delta for dedicated? we got the initial estimate but it's still fuzzy for finance.
[01:40] Sofia Patel: sure, i'll talk numbers in the cost section, but short answer: dedicated reduces per-token cost by about 20-35% for steady throughput while giving the p99 SLA. For bursty workloads you pay for reserved headroom unless you enable burst capacity. we can send a dedicated pilot proposal with committed hours so it's more predictable.
[01:55] Maya Singh: security here - before we consider private deployment we need SOC2 scope confirmation and KMS/HSM integration details. also encryption at rest needs to meet our policy. do you have a security pack?
[02:06] Jordan Kim: yes, we do. we'll send the security pack and also a tighter SOC2 scope doc specific to private deployments. Sofia will include it in the follow up.
[02:15] Aisha Malik: one question — what changed between your hosted runtime versions? our engineers saw a new kernel landing around mid-november, could that be related?
[02:22] Marcus Li: we did push a change to improve attention speed for long context, but it shouldn't have regressed latency; it was gated and rolled out to 10% first. i'll double-check rollout windows — maybe that overlapped with your scoring job.
[02:38] Tom Reyes: even if rollout overlap, we need isolation. dedicated would solve that, but we want to quantify cost. also curious about model version pinning for staged rollouts. can the platform do canary for model variants?
[02:50] Marcus Li: yes, rollouts support canary and automatic fallback. you can pin a route to a version and set automatic fallback to a faster quantized variant if latency breaches threshold. low fidelity warning: sometimes the name of the quantized variant shows up oddly in our UI (autogen shows 'q4_0-lite' as 'q4lite' in older dashboards) — minor UX thing.
[03:12] Chris (Data Eng): joining now, link to the trace: http://tiny.link/trace-nov12 (note to self: link will be replaced in final notes).
[03:20] Sofia Patel: thanks chris. ok moving into costs — i'll screen-share the quick model cost breakout. our calc shows the Nov spike added ~38% incremental token cost for Week 2, mostly from the nightly job being mis-scheduled and no prefix caching.
[03:40] Ben Ortiz: so the immediate fixes are scheduler change + caching?
[03:44] Marcus Li: yep, and also lowering maximum sequence length for that job, and enabling prefix/KV cache for repeated prompts; in our tests that reduced tokens by ~28% on similar workloads.
[04:00] Aisha Malik: do you have an example config for the cache? we want something we can drop into k8s cronjob.
[04:06] Marcus Li: i'll share a sample config in the repo, it's a small yaml and a best-practice doc. Jordan will include in the security pack link as well.
[04:20] Maya Singh: regarding private deployment: our blockers are audit logs retention, KMS integrations, and network egress policies. can you confirm the private option supports customer-managed KMS?
[04:32] Jordan Kim: yes, private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM. we also support per-request audit logs and can integrate with your SIEM. i'll add the retention window options to the doc.
[04:48] Tom Reyes: timelines — if we want a POC for dedicated, how quickly can you spin a pilot? we have a seasonal traffic window in mid-december so ideally to test before that.
[04:55] Sofia Patel: operationally we can spin a 4-week dedicated pilot within 7-10 business days once the contract is signed and we get billing details. that gets you predictable capacity for the mid-decident window.
[05:06] Aisha Malik: mid-december is tight — we need results by Dec 14. is that feasible?
[05:10] Marcus Li: yes, if contract signed by Dec 1 and configs provided. timeline lines up.
[05:18] Ben Ortiz: on the SLA side, can we get p99 target and credits if missed?
[05:22] Sofia Patel: standard dedicated SLA includes p99 targets and partial credits for sustained misses; we can add a custom SLA for larger commitments — we'll include language in the pilot contract.
[05:30] Priya Anand: can you outline what metrics you'll collect during the pilot? we need API-level traces, GPU utilization, per-route token counts.
[05:38] Marcus Li: absolutely — we'll collect p50/p95/p99 latencies, per-route token counts, GPU util, batch sizes, KV cache hit rate, and failure rates. results will be posted to the shared benchmark sheet.
[05:55] Aisha Malik: another ask: model rollout governance — we want a gate that prevents auto-rollout to prod if eval metrics drop. is that supported?
[06:03] Marcus Li: yes we have eval hooks and rollback policies tied to prompt-based eval sets. you define pass/fail thresholds and the platform can auto-rollback. it's in the rollout docs but we'll give you a lanecrest sample.
[06:20] Sofia Patel: ok, quick recap of recommended short-term cost wins: 1) reschedule nightly scoring away from peak, 2) enable prefix caching on repeated prompts, 3) reduce sequence length for scoring job, 4) add a small dedicated pool for critical routes during peak. those are ordered by effort -> impact.
[06:40] Tom Reyes: any risks with prefix caching vis-a-vis PII? could caching store sensitive tokens?
[06:46] Maya Singh: exactly — we need to ensure caching honors redaction rules and TTLs.
[06:51] Marcus Li: caching is configurable; you can set tokenization redaction and TTLs and opt out for specific routes. we'll include the security knobs in the doc.
[07:05] Chris (Data Eng): note: our trace shows a pattern of repeated prefixes from the nightly job — caching would help a lot.
[07:10] Sofia Patel: great. quick poll: are folks comfortable with Redwood running a 48h benchmark and sharing results?
[07:15] Tom Reyes: yes please do.
[07:17] Aisha Malik: yes.
[07:18] Ben Ortiz: yes.
[07:19] Maya Singh: yes but need the security pack before any infra-level access.
[07:22] Sofia Patel: understood — security pack first. Jordan will send.
[07:30] Jordan Kim: i'll share the security pack and a SOC2 scope doc to maya and aisha right after the call, also include KMS/HSM integration details and audit log options.
[07:40] Sofia Patel: action items — i'll own pricing and pilot template. Marcus will own the benchmark. jordan owns security pack. lanecrest to provide logs and stakeholder list.
[07:55] Aisha Malik: one more ask — we have internal compliance review on Dec 8; can you have the security doc in hand by Dec 3?
[08:02] Jordan Kim: yes we'll aim for Dec 3.
[08:10] Marcus Li: small technical note: the p99 spike looked like memory thrash due to an older quantization path; i'll try to reproduce locally with the same model variant and traffic, may find a quickfix.
[08:25] Sofia Patel: perfect. let's go to quick Q&A, then wrap.
[08:30] Ben Ortiz: question — what about autoscaling latency? we saw autoscaler spin up but initial requests still hit cold caches. can dedicated help here?
[08:40] Marcus Li: dedicated reduces cold-start variance because e.g., GPUs are warm and pre-warm caches. autoscaling cold path still exists but with dedicated reserved nodes it's less likely to impact p99.
[08:54] Priya Anand: we still want guidance on autoscaler configs — graceful draining, min nodes, etc.
[08:59] Marcus Li: we'll include suggested autoscaler settings for Lanecrest's traffic profile.
[09:12] Aisha Malik: ok thanks folks, this was useful. can you confirm next steps in an email with the links and timelines?
[09:20] Sofia Patel: yes we'll send a follow-up summary and include the contract template + security pack + sample cache config + benchmark plan. expect that by EOD tomorrow.
[09:30] Tom Reyes: thanks everyone.

End of recording.
